title: Fix it and prove it
summary: Change the code, the Collector and the alert rules the way a team would, then show the fix in the same graphs that showed the problem.

steps.title: Every fix has a proof
body: The second half of the shift changes things, in three places:
- **the code** (`/app/src/Program.cs` on the shop node: saving rebuilds and redeploys): a missing attribute, an unbounded one;
- **the Collector** (`/work/collector/config.yaml`: validated, then restarted): redaction for every service at once;
- **the alert rules** (`/work/prometheus/rules/`: `promtool check rules`, then `POST /-/reload`): a page that means something;
- and finally **the database**, the cause of ticket 2, proved with the latency panel.
For each, before you press **Check**, say which graph, trace or query proves it. That sentence is what goes in the incident channel.

steps.prompt: You created the index. What is the proof the incident is over?
options: p95 of the product route over the last few minutes is back under the objective, on the same panel that showed the problem
The trace of one request was fast
Nobody has complained for ten minutes
steps.explain: An aggregate over real traffic, compared with the objective. One fast trace is an anecdote; silence is not data.

steps.title: Ticket 6: add the attribute the team needs
steps.prompt: Add `app.cart.size` (an integer) to the checkout span in the shop's code.

steps.title: Ticket 7: personal data in the traces
steps.prompt: Hash or delete `user.email` in the Collector's traces pipeline.
steps.explain: A processor only runs when a pipeline lists it.

steps.title: Ticket 8: an alert that pages for the right reason
steps.prompt: Write the multiwindow burn-rate alert, retire the noisy one, check and reload.
steps.explain: Symptoms, budgets, two windows, a runbook.

steps.title: Ticket 9: the metric that ate Prometheus
steps.prompt: Remove the unbounded attribute from `app.orders` in code.
steps.explain: Bounded labels on metrics; ids on spans.

steps.title: Ticket 10: fix the slow page, and prove it
steps.prompt: Add the index the product query needs, then prove p95 dropped under 25 ms.
